question: What evidence does the Commission seek under Article 4(1)(c) and (d) of Directive (EU) 2022/20411 when assessing whether Ireland provides effective protection against discrimination and interference for workers and trade unions wishing to participate in collective bargaining on wage-setting, including before formal trade union recognition has been established?
How will the Commission assess the availability of effective remedies for employees seeking such representation in the workplace?
Does the Commission believe that the protections and remedies available under Irish law are effective in practice at the point when employees begin seeking collective bargaining?
Directive (EU) 2022/2041 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 19 October 2022 on adequate minimum wages in the European Union, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/dir/2022/2041/oj. 1
